entities.text: Maddukuri Gopi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2019 
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6059 Of 2019
Order:

1. In this Criminal Petition, filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the Petitioners/A2 and A4 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.556 of 2019 of Gajuwaka Police Station,
Visakhapatnam city, which was registered against them and others for the offences under Sections 328, 188 and 273 R/w.34 of IPC and Section 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short,
'the FSS Act').
2.

The allegations against the Petitioners/A2 and A4, briefly, are that on 26.09.2019 at 15:30 hours,
when the complainant along with his staff proceeded to D.No.17-6-25, near Durga Temple,
Kandipalli street, Pedagantyada, found A-2 and A-4 in possession of banned tobacco products, who are working in the shop of Shiva Manikanta Enterprises belonging to A-3, who purchased the same from Odisha and selling the same at Visakhapatnam on a higher rate, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products,
seized the same, registered F.I.R., remanded them to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore UDPR,J registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub- Inspector of Police, Gajuwaka Police Station, Visakhapatnam City.

Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

sentences.text:
Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the Petitioners/A2 and A4 for the offences under Sections 188,
273 and 328 R/w.34 of IPC and Section 59 of the FSS Act are hereby quashed.
6. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.

U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J Date: 01.10.2019 DSH Maddukuri Gopi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40142471/
